pgVector.intro: LiteLLM provides a server to connect to PG Vector. To use this provider:

steps.configure: Configure your PostgreSQL database with pgvector extension
steps.start: Start the server and note the API base URL and API key
steps.enter: Enter those details in the fields below

valkey.title: Valkey Setup Required
valkey.intro: LiteLLM searches documents you have already stored in Valkey. It does not create the index or upload documents for you. Before creating this vector store, make sure:

steps.searchEnabled: Your Valkey server has vector search enabled (the valkey-search module, included in the valkey-bundle image and in AWS ElastiCache / MemoryDB for Valkey)
steps.indexLoaded: You have already created a search index and loaded your documents and their embeddings into it. Enter that index name as the Vector Store ID
steps.embeddingModel: You know which embedding model created those stored embeddings. That model must be added to this proxy under Models so you can pick it below. Using a different model returns wrong results
steps.fieldNames: You know the field names your documents use for their text and their embedding. If they are not "text" and "embedding", set them below

valkey.howItWorks: When a query comes in, LiteLLM converts it to an embedding with the model below and returns the closest matching documents from your index.

opensearch.title: OpenSearch Setup Required
opensearch.intro: LiteLLM searches a k-NN index you already have in an OpenSearch Serverless collection or an OpenSearch Service domain. It does not create the index or upload documents. Before creating this vector store, make sure:

steps.knnField: The index has a knn_vector field holding each document's embedding. Enter the index name as the Vector Store ID, or under Index Name when another endpoint already uses that ID
steps.embeddingModel: You know which embedding model created those embeddings. That model must be added to this proxy under Models so you can pick it below. Using a different model returns wrong results
steps.credentials: The proxy has AWS credentials that can read the index, either its own (environment variables or an IAM role) or a saved credential picked under Existing Credentials. A Serverless collection needs a data access policy for them, and a domain needs its access policy to allow them

vertexRagEngine.title: Vertex AI RAG Engine Setup
vertexRagEngine.intro: To use Vertex AI RAG Engine:
vertexRagEngine.renameNote: Note: Google Cloud has renamed this to "RAG Engine" in its console — the steps below still apply.

steps.guide: Set up your Vertex AI RAG Engine corpus following the guide: <guide>Vertex AI RAG Engine Overview</guide>
steps.createCorpus: Create a corpus in your Google Cloud project
steps.noteCorpusId: Note the corpus ID from the Vertex AI console (now labeled "RAG Engine" in Google Cloud)
steps.enterCorpusId: Enter the corpus ID in the Vector Store ID field below

vertexAiSearch.title: Vertex AI Search Setup
vertexAiSearch.intro: To use Vertex AI Search (Discovery Engine):
vertexAiSearch.renameNote: Note: Google Cloud has renamed this to "Agent Search" in its console — the steps below still apply.

steps.guide: Enable the Discovery Engine API on your Google Cloud project and create a data store following the guide: <guide>Create a Vertex AI Search data store</guide>
steps.location: Pick a supported location: global, us, or eu
steps.dataStoreId: For most data store types (Cloud Storage, BigQuery, Media): copy the data store ID and enter it in the Vector Store ID field below.
steps.engineId: For website, healthcare, and connector-based sources (Drive, Gmail, Slack, Jira, etc.): create a search app on top of the data store, then copy the Engine ID and enter it in the Engine ID field. The Vector Store ID is still required as the LiteLLM-side name for this record, but it isn't used in the GCP URL when Engine ID is set.

pgVector.apiBase: Enter the base URL of your deployed litellm-pgvector server (e.g., http://your-server:8000)
pgVector.apiKey: Enter the API key from your deployed litellm-pgvector server

vertexAiSearch.project: Google Cloud project ID that hosts the Vertex AI Search data store.
vertexAiSearch.location: Vertex AI Search data store location. Must be one of global, us, or eu.
vertexAiSearch.collectionId: Discovery Engine collection ID. Leave blank to use the default collection.
vertexAiSearch.engineId: Search app (engine) ID. Required for website, healthcare, and connector-based data stores (Workspace, Slack, Jira, etc.) because these sources route search through an engine. Leave blank to query the data store directly.

azure.apiKey: Enter your Azure OpenAI API key
azure.apiBase: Enter your Azure OpenAI endpoint (e.g., https://your-resource.openai.azure.com/)

milvus.apiKey: To obtain a token, you should use a colon (:) to concatenate the username and password that you use to access your Milvus instance (e.g., username:password)
milvus.embeddingModel: Select the embedding model to use

mongodb.apiBase: Use HTTPS for a remote sidecar, or HTTP with a loopback IP for a sidecar on the same host or Pod
mongodb.apiKey: The MONGODB_SIDECAR_API_KEY configured in your MongoDB sidecar
mongodb.database: The MongoDB database holding the collection you want to search
mongodb.collection: The collection your MongoDB Vector Search index was built on
mongodb.embeddingModel: The embedding model on this proxy that created the vectors already stored in your collection. LiteLLM embeds every search query with it, so it must be the same model. A different model of the same size will not error, it will just return wrong results. Add it under Models first if it is not listed
mongodb.embeddingField: The field in each document that holds its embedding. It must match the path your MongoDB Vector Search index was created on (default: embedding)
mongodb.textField: The field in each document that holds its readable text. LiteLLM returns this text in search results, and it accepts a dotted path such as metadata.body (default: text)
mongodb.numCandidates: How many nearest neighbours MongoDB examines before returning the top results. Higher is more accurate and slower. Leave blank to let LiteLLM scale it with the requested result count

valkey.host: Hostname or IP of your Valkey server, without redis:// or a port (e.g. my-valkey.example.com)
valkey.port: Port your Valkey server listens on. Leave as 6379 unless you changed it
valkey.password: Password used to log in to your Valkey server. Leave blank if it has no password
valkey.ssl: Set to true if your Valkey server requires an encrypted (TLS) connection, for example AWS ElastiCache with in-transit encryption turned on
valkey.embeddingModel: The embedding model on this proxy that was used to create the embeddings already stored in your Valkey index. LiteLLM uses it to embed each search query, so it must be the same model or results will be wrong. Add it under Models first if it is not listed
valkey.textField: The field in each stored document that holds its readable text. LiteLLM returns this text in search results. Must match how your documents were stored (default: text)
valkey.embeddingField: The field in each stored document that holds its embedding. LiteLLM searches against this field, so it must match the field your index was created on (default: embedding)

opensearch.apiBase: The endpoint of your OpenSearch Serverless collection or OpenSearch Service domain, starting with https://
opensearch.region: The AWS region of the collection or domain. Leave blank to use the region in the endpoint, and set it when the endpoint is a custom domain
opensearch.embeddingModel: The embedding model on this proxy that created the vectors already stored in your index. LiteLLM embeds every search query with it, so it must be the same model. Add it under Models first if it is not listed
opensearch.embeddingField: The top-level knn_vector field in your index mapping that holds each document's embedding (default: embedding)
opensearch.textField: The top-level field in each document that holds its readable text. LiteLLM returns this text in search results (default: text)
opensearch.indexName: The OpenSearch index to search. Leave blank to use the Vector Store ID, and set it to register same-named indexes from two endpoints under different IDs

s3Vectors.bucketName: S3 bucket name for vector storage (will be auto-created if it doesn't exist)
s3Vectors.indexName: Name for the vector index (optional, will be auto-generated if not provided)
s3Vectors.region: AWS region where the S3 bucket is located (e.g., us-west-2)
s3Vectors.embeddingModel: Select the embedding model to use for vector generation

aboutAttachments.title: About Policy Attachments
aboutAttachments.description: Policy attachments control where your policies apply. Policies don't do anything until you attach them to specific teams, keys, models, tags, or globally.

scopes.keys: Keys - Applies only to specific API keys (supports wildcards like dev-*)
scopes.models: Models - Applies only when specific models are used
scopes.tags: Tags - Matches tags from key/team metadata.tags or tags passed dynamically in the request body (metadata.tags). Use this to enforce policies across groups, e.g. "all keys tagged healthcare get HIPAA guardrails." Supports wildcards (prod-*).
